### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8caa131e52717ef35fe71742d758f10b8f2b77ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2de71f32cd64d6d1f7f97567ddc15f0f989699bb` — the merge of head `cf854f71dc379b62288390cd779476586644db3b` into base `8caa131e52717ef35fe71742d758f10b8f2b77ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2de71f32cd64d6d1f7f97567ddc15f0f989699bb && git checkout 2de71f32cd64d6d1f7f97567ddc15f0f989699bb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8caa131e52717ef35fe71742d758f10b8f2b77ee cf854f71dc379b62288390cd779476586644db3b && git checkout -B drift-repro 8caa131e52717ef35fe71742d758f10b8f2b77ee && git merge --no-ff cf854f71dc379b62288390cd779476586644db3b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8caa131e52717ef35fe71742d758f10b8f2b77ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `eb2152b86bc87606a968a6ff00ca9084b951ab20`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22044 (body; triage `6028457956`; claim `6029104290`; dev report `6030118362`), PR #22048 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the merge-base `9a0401fd`: 4 files, +61/−5), the 32 check-runs on the head, and the two checkouts through `git show` only (objectstack at `origin/main` and the head, objectui at `c0862c1c`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: none changes. Right.** The only `src/` edit is `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, and every changed byte there is comment text: two `/* @__PURE__ */` markers and two docblocks. No schema, conversion, order, id or value moves; `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`, `inApplicationOrder` and the rows of `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` are untouched. Triage's guard (every entry keeps its export list) holds by construction, and the PR body's parity readings are consistent with it: `check:api-surface` exit 0; 48 entry files / 7,864 runtime names with 0 differing, against a 17.6.0 control leg reading 16; 228 `dist/` files on both sides. The shipped `api-surface/*.json` lists names and kinds only (`ALL_CONVERSIONS (const)`), so it needs no regeneration; the PR touches no generated artifact and `check:generated` is reported green.

**Public surface, what reaches a published file. Right, with one precision note.** `files[]` ships `dist/**` and `src/**/*.zod.ts`. `registry.ts` is not a `.zod.ts`, so the source itself is not shipped, but it is bundled into every entry whose graph reaches it: `conversions/index.ts` line 26 re-exports it, `src/index.ts` line 227 re-exports conversions, and `./shared` reaches it through `shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts` → `conversions/apply.ts` → `registry.ts`. So the two markers land in `dist/shared/index.mjs`, the root, `dist/browser/**` and every other entry carrying the table, and in their `.mjs.map`. The docblocks of two exported consts also change, so if the DTS pass emits JSDoc the `.d.mts` text moves too; the declared types do not. The changeset's "every declaration and every runtime value is unchanged" is true of the declarations, and "only the bytes a bundler keeps change" is true of the runtime bundles. Not blocking.

**Where each annotation sits, and which call it covers. Right.**
- esbuild 0.28.x (tsup's first pass): a `@__PURE__` comment applies to the call or new expression that follows it together with its whole postfix chain, so `/* @__PURE__ */ a().b()` marks `a().b()`. For `ALL_CONVERSIONS` the marked node is therefore the outermost `.flatMap(...)` call; when it is unused esbuild drops the call and ignores its target (the inner `Object.keys(...).map(Number).sort(...)`), examining only the outermost call's argument, an arrow function. For row `18` the marked node is `inApplicationOrder(MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS)`, whose one argument is a module-bound identifier. esbuild re-emits a marker it parsed, which is why each entry carrying the table grows by exactly 32 raw bytes, two 16-byte prefixes.
- Rollup 4.62.2 (tsup 8.5.1's `treeshake: true` second pass, `renderChunk` through `rollup()`): `CallExpression.hasEffects` checks the arguments and then returns false on `annotationPure` without visiting the callee, so the chain under the marked call is never examined, and the comment survives as source text. With `preserveEntrySignatures: 'exports-only'` this pass keeps every export of the entry, so nothing is dropped at publish time: `./shared` still exports `normalizeStackInput`, which reads the table.
- Rolldown: objectui's console at `c0862c1c` builds with Vite 8.2.2, whose lockfile dependency is `rolldown 1.2.7`; the report's per-entry probe ran rolldown 1.0.3. Both are measured in the report (registry.ts 201,720 → 0 bytes in the `./shared` probe; 129 ids × 2 → × 0 in `vendor-objectstack`), not re-run here.
- Why source annotations rather than the `pure-schema-construction` plugin: the plugin marks by callee name (`lazySchema`, `strictObject`, `defineForm`) across `src/`; `map`, `sort`, `flatMap` and `Object.keys` cannot join that set without marking every such call in the package. Two explicit marks are the narrowest change. Right.

**Are the two calls free of side effects? Yes.** `inApplicationOrder` copies its argument (`[...entries]`), sorts the copy by `order` then `id`, and maps to the conversion; it reads nothing outside its argument, mutates nothing it does not own, and cannot throw on the table as authored. The `ALL_CONVERSIONS` chain reads `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` and sorts the fresh array `.map(Number)` returned. The other rows of the object literal are array literals of module-bound consts, so once row 18 is pure the whole initializer is removable when unread, and the 129 conversion objects and the schemas only they reference go with it. In Node nothing is bundled and the marker is a comment: both calls run exactly as before, so no observable behaviour changes anywhere; in a bundle, a dropped table is one nothing reads.

**The pin, `scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts`. Right, with one finding.**
- Positive control: yes. The `normalizeStackInput` consumer must keep all 129 ids (`toEqual(ids)`) and `ids.length` must exceed 100, so a broken instrument (table externalised, empty import, no tree-shaking) reds the control instead of passing the console case vacuously. The report's reverse verification (each marker removed in turn through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, the pin red with 129 and then 62 ids kept, restored to blob `d707d83fdbad`) is at `08392e53a4`, which shares this head's `src/` and `scripts/` tree.
- It builds from `src/` through tsup with the package's `mainConfig` (same plugin, `splitting: false`, `treeshake: true`), so no `dist/` sits between source and assertion. It belongs to the spec `local` vitest project (`scripts/**/*.test.ts` minus the repo list), the project `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` and CI's Test Core run.
- Names: objectui at `c0862c1c` value-imports FIVE names from `@objectstack/spec/shared` in non-test source: `canonicalMetaUrlType` (app-shell `DraftChangesPanel.tsx`, `studioScope.ts`), `ValueDomainSchema` (`ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`), `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED` and `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` (`flow-sim-validate.ts`), `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` and `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` (`@object-ui/types` `zod/base.zod.ts`, `zod/form.zod.ts`); every other import is `import type`. The pin's console consumer names three (`EvaluatedExpressionSchema, ValueDomainSchema, canonicalMetaUrlType`), while the report's own consumer probe used "the console's 5 names". The two names the pin omits are both defined in `src/shared/expression.zod.ts`, whose only imports are `zod` and `./refinement-projection` (which imports nothing), so no statement in that module can reach the table and the pin's `[]` verdict is the same with five names as with three. Wrong as a description ("imports what objectui's console imports"), not a coverage hole. Carried to ③.

**`WIRING` in `scripts/conversions-major18-merge.test.ts`. Intact.** The constant is matched against the raw `SOURCE` slice of `export const CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` (not the comment-masked text), beside `not.toMatch(/^ {2}18: \[/m)`, so the test still proves row 18 is read through `inApplicationOrder(MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS)` and is not an appendable array. `entriesOf` scans the `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` list, which the diff does not touch, so the seven merge fixtures and the four lit controls are unchanged. No other script, skill or doc quotes the wiring line textually (grep over the head tree: the registry, this test and the changeset only).

**`Fixes #22044`: meets the card once released.** The card's acceptance is a release carrying the reduction, with the recovered bytes measured. The measurement is done with the card's instrument (`apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, objectui `c0862c1c`): eager closure −226,238 gzip, `vendor-objectstack` 1,604,719 → 1,378,418 gzip, table copies 2 → 0, repeatable, against the +182,909 the 17.7.0 bump added. The release act is the maintainer's under Prime Directive #15 and cannot be in the PR; the `patch` changeset routes the change into the next Version Packages PR, which is the placement triage set. Closing at merge matches the precedent (#20646) and the card's own text, which leaves the ceiling lowering to objectui once that release resolves. The two card checks ("Part-of PR must not also close its card", "The card this PR closes must claim this branch") are green.

**Check-runs on the head, as read once, not polled:** 32 in all. 14 `success`: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, filter, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates. 3 `skipped`: Build Docs; Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in, not owed since the chunk layout does not move); Console Pin Gate (its `console` filter lists only `packages/spec/package.json` and `tsup.config.ts` among spec paths, because the rest of the spec is cached content by ruled design, so the skip is the filter's, and the console reading is the report's local one above). 15 `in_progress`: Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6, Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. 0 `failure`. Landing waits for every one of them regardless of this record.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22044-shared-entry-drops-conversion-table.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **`patch`**. Right. The diff publishes bytes from a released package (the markers in every `dist/**` bundle carrying the table), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; it adds no feature and changes no contract, so `minor` is not owed. `Clause-②: no`, no arm, on both the PR body and the changeset body: well-formed and true, since no accept set widens or narrows and no export, declaration or runtime value moves. The changeset text was checked sentence by sentence: the path `./shared` → `normalizeStackInput` → `applyConversions` → `ALL_CONVERSIONS` is the only non-test import path from `src/shared/**` into `conversions/registry.ts` at this head (the other non-test importers are `migrations/*`, which `./shared` does not reach); the named readers are readers (`defineStack` in `stack.zod.ts` line 3892 calls `normalizeStackInput`; `applyConversions` iterates `ALL_CONVERSIONS`); the console figure matches the report. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report deviations, each answered:
1. Candidate injected through objectui's own `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` rather than a packed tarball. Accepted: it is the Console Pin Gate's injection, and the (a) against (b) control (+248 gzip, main's drift since the tag) shows the path moves the control by noise; (b) − (c) isolates the fix.
2. Route is a source annotation, not `tsup.config.ts`. Within the claim's file surface: `registry.ts` is the `src/**` module the measurement named, and the edit changes how the table is emitted, not any shape, accept set or `.describe()` text; and it is the narrower route (① above). The file set and chunk layout do not move, so `publish-smoke` and `needs:pack-smoke` are not owed.
3. `-- --maxWorkers=2` dropped by vitest. The whole `local` project ran at default workers; no effect on the readings.
4. Long builds under `os-verify-lock.sh` via nohup. Process hygiene; no effect.
5. Harness attribution against AGENTS.md. The three commits carry exactly the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes (`Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`), and the PR body carries the session-URL footer; the report's choice is the rule's. Nothing to correct.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

`out_of_scope_findings`, both "carrier: none, noted, not filed": accepted as out of scope, with one steer.
- The 47,491 gzip that `./shared` still keeps for the console's names (side-effectful arguments inside PURE-marked `strictObject` calls: bare `z.*` chains, `.optional().describe(…)` on imported schemas, `componentSlot(…)`) is a measured, reproducible lead for the next payback, not a defect. Whether to file it is the dispatching seat's call, not a condition of this record.
- One `component.zod.ts` copy per flat entry is the `splitting: false` design; the shared-chunk route redraws the published file set, and the `tsup.config.ts` docblock asks for that review first. Correctly left alone.

Reviewer's own flags:
- **Pin names, follow-up owed, not blocking.** The console consumer in the pin should name all five value-imported names: add `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED` and `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` to the string, so the test comment and the PR body's "the names objectui's console imports from `./shared`" read true. The pin's verdict does not change (same module closure, shown in ①), and the PR's measured claims do not rest on it.
- The `.d.mts` docblock text of `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` and `ALL_CONVERSIONS` moves if the DTS pass emits JSDoc; the report's order-insensitive declaration-tree comparison reads identical, which is consistent with a comparison that normalises comments. Declared types are unchanged either way. Noted, not blocking.
- objectui's half (ceiling and `BASELINE` down by the (b) − (c) reading) is objectui's follow-up once it resolves the release, as the card and triage already state; no objectui commit was made. Nothing to escalate.
